sentences.text: TAHSIL

JUNNARDEO DISTRICT CHHINDWARA  (MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI A.T.FARIDI - ADVOCATE)
 AND  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH THROUGH THE  POLICE STATION JUNNARDEO R/O DISTRICT  CHHINDWARA (MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI A.S.PATHAK - GOVT. ADVOCATE)
 This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER

This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.42/2023 registered at Police Station-Junnardeo District-Chhindwara (MP) for the offence under Sections 304(B), 498A of IPC &
3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
2. Learned counsel appearing for the applicant submitted that applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
It is submitted that Archana fell down in a drain, while she was feeding pet animals.
She received injury on her head.
She was immediately taken to hospital.
Later on, she succumbed to the injuries.
It is submitted that only general allegations of harassment is made against applicant and no particulars are given.
In these circumstances, prayer is made to enlarge applicant on bail.

sentences.text: 3. Learned Government Advocate appearing for the State opposed the application for grant of bail.
It is submitted that applicant has assaulted the deceased with a stick on her head, which later on resulted in death.
Applicant was demanding Rs.10 lacs of dowry.
Applicant also used to harass the deceased.
In these circumstances, bail application may be dismissed.

4. Heard the counsel for the parties.
5.
As per prosecution story, applicant is said to have assaulted the deceased on his head with a stick but however, no offence under Section 302 of IPC is alleged against applicant in charge-sheet.
Further, on going through the statement of relatives, it is found that general allegations of harassment was made.
Particulars of date and time, when harassment was done, was not mentioned and it was also not been mentioned that Archana had told relatives regarding beating or harassment by applicant.
6. Considering facts and circumstances of the case, bail application filed by applicant is allowed.
It is directed that applicant be released on bail on furnishing personal bond of Rs.50,000/-(Rs.Fifty Thousand only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court.
7. The applicant shall also abide by the following conditions of Section 437 (3) of Cr. P. C. C.C. as per rules.

(VISHAL DHAGAT) JUDGE nd Omkar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5540118/
